title: Evaluation of the long-term safety and effectiveness of intraocular lenses.
summary:
Surgery to remove the natural lens of the eye in the context of cataracts or clear lens exchange (lens replacement in the case of diminished accommodation capacity) is one of the most common medical procedures of all. Today, it is usually performed on an outpatient basis and requires the implantation of an artificial intraocular lens (IOL) after removal of the crystalline lens.
Choosing the right IOL is one of the biggest challenges for the surgeon, as there are various intraocular lenses with different designs and materials available that allow patients to have good vision at distance, intermediate and near distances 1-3 after lens surgery. One of the most common complications after lens surgery is posterior capsule opacification (PCO). Deterioration of vision due to PCO occurs in 20-40% of patients after 2-5 years, with younger patients being affected more frequently than older patients4, as well as patients with glaucoma or a previous vitrectomy5,6. 
Preventively, various surgical techniques, lens materials and designs have been developed7-10 to prevent PCO. However, it can only be treated by neodymium : YAG (Nd : YAG) laser capsulotomy. The incidence of Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy increases the longer it has been since lens surgery11.
Changes in the lens material (for example due to small water-filled microvacuoles, known as glistening14) can also lead to vision loss15,16.
In the present study, long-term results on patient satisfaction and visual performance with different intraocular lenses are to be collected, with particular consideration of any changes to these.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Pseudophakia
- Patients aged 30 years and older 	
- Treatment with an intraocular lens implanted in the capsular bag
- Signed informed consent form, whereby the subjects have been informed in detail about the purpose of the study and participate voluntarily
- Presence of preoperative data
Exclusion criteria:
- none
